# Embassy v1.7.0 — more providers, less machinery

Two things happened in this release, and they are the same thing seen from two sides: **Embassy became an N-provider gateway** — Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek, and Grok Build, twelve routable directions, every one behind an explicit consent edge — and **the codebase got about 8,500 lines smaller** while doing it.

New providers ride ACP, the open Agent Client Protocol. Embassy's client is deliberately minimal: four outbound methods, two served handlers, permission requests always denied, all five stop reasons preserved uncollapsed, and one invented terminal state — `UNKNOWN`, for the transport dying with a prompt outstanding, because a dead pipe proves nothing and Embassy refuses to guess. Grok Build launches from the ACP registry's checksummed exact pin. DeepSeek launches from a local harness checkout, and its lane ships with a deliberately humble receipt: that adapter collapses aborted, blocked, and error outcomes into `end_turn` upstream, so Embassy settles those `unconfirmed` with `ACP_OUTCOME_COARSE` rather than claim a delivery it cannot prove. A genuine cancellation still settles `cancelled`.

The removal is the bigger story. Online certification is gone in full — evidence tiers, boot probes, certification APIs, version-gated quarantine, the write-attestation probe, the two-factor write gate. What a release was tested with now lives in one release-owned support matrix that the running broker provably never imports; what runtime claims is only what this connection, this route, and this correlated operation demonstrated. Version strings are unverified metadata everywhere. Nothing about the trust model moved: per-edge consent, broker-owned provenance envelopes, OS-boundary attestation, and the anti-runaway bounds are all intact, and the ambiguity law — never replay a possibly-written message — now extends across four providers.

One breaking change, stated plainly: persisted state is schema v2, and pre-v1.7 state fails strict parsing with a clear error instead of migrating silently. A single-user install re-pairs once after upgrading — two commands per route, a few minutes, and the fresh state exercises the new registration paths.

Verification: the full suite and deliverability soak green on every landed slice from isolated worktrees; an offline ACP protocol-core conformance suite (framing, correlation, generation isolation, cancel races, process-death phases, no-replay) now anchors the per-harness release gate; a credential sentinel proves the DeepSeek launch path never reads harness credentials; and the live drill on the published artifact covers the state cutover and re-pair.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.7.0`, stop your broker, move the old state file aside, start the broker, re-register and re-pair your routes.
